name: Last One
description: Last One (also known as Last Card) is a popular shedding-type card game from the Crazy Eights family. Played across many Commonwealth countries, particularly New Zealand and Australia, it involves players trying to empty their hands by matching cards on a central pile. The game is famous for its 'special cards' that force opponents to draw or skip turns, and the mandatory requirement to announce 'Last One' when holding a single card.

overview.description: Last One (also known as Last Card) is a popular shedding-type card game from the Crazy Eights family. Played across many Commonwealth countries, particularly New Zealand and Australia, it involves players trying to empty their hands by matching cards on a central pile. The game is famous for its 'special cards' that force opponents to draw or skip turns, and the mandatory requirement to announce 'Last One' when holding a single card.

history.origins: Dates to the early 20th century as a localized expansion of Crazy Eights. It gained popularity in New Zealand, Australia, the UK, and parts of the United States as a faster, more aggressive social game.
timeline: 1930s: Mau-Mau and Crazy Eights rules consolidate in Europe and America.
1960s: 'Last One' becomes a standard schoolyard and pub game in New Zealand and Australia.
1971: The commercial game UNO is released, which is essentially a streamlined, proprietary version of Last One/Crazy Eights.
1980s: Traced back to Walla Walla prison in Washington State, USA, according to some sources.
Present: Remains a common generic card game known by various regional names worldwide.
history.cultural: In New Zealand, it is almost exclusively known as 'Last Card' and is a staple of school lunch breaks and family gatherings. The game serves as an introduction to card games for many children due to its simple rules and exciting special cards.
history.evolution: The game evolved to have 'stackable' penalties, where multiple 2s played in sequence can force a player to draw 4, 6, or more cards. The 'Last Card' announcement rule was formalized to prevent players from sneaking out a win.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck + 2 Jokers. Jokers are typically 'Draw 5' or 'Draw 6' penalty cards.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 cards (or 4-9 cards at dealer's choice). One card is turned up to start the discard pile. Remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard deck and a flat surface.

rules.objective: The object is to be the first player to have no cards left in your hand; the first to empty their hand wins the round.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing a card to the discard pile that matches the previous card in rank OR suit. If unable to play, draw one card from the stock. If the drawn card is playable, it may be played immediately.
keyRules: Two (2): Next player draws 2 cards and loses their turn. Multiple 2s can be stacked (e.g., two 2s = draw 4).
Three (3): May be played on any card and allows the player to play another card immediately (stacking).
Four (4): Causes a 'melee'â€”the next player must play a 5 of the same suit if possible, then 6, etc. If the sequence stops, the current target draws cards equal to the last played rank.
Eight (8): Wild card. Can be played on any card. Player announces a new suit that must be followed.
Jack (J): Skip the next player's turn.
Ace (A): Reverse direction of play. In 2-player games, acts as a Skip.
Joker: Next player draws 5 cards (or 6, by agreement) and loses their turn. Cannot be stacked in most rules.

Last Card Rule: When a player has exactly one card left, they MUST say 'Last One' (or 'Last Card'). If another player catches them not saying it before the next card is played, the offender must draw a penalty card (usually 1 or 2).

strategy.basic: Keep your 'Wild cards' (8s and Jokers) for your final few turns. Using an 8 as your last card is the safest way to win because you don't need to worry about the suit on the pile. Save penalty cards (2s, Jokers) for when opponents have few cards.
strategy.intermediate: The Draw Trap: If a player to your right says 'Last One', and you have a 2 or a Joker, play it immediately! This forces them to draw cards and ruins their chance of winning on their next turn. Also, use 8s strategically to change to a suit where you hold multiple cards.
strategy.advanced: Suit Control: If you have many cards of one suit and see your opponent keeps drawing when that suit is on top, keep playing that suit. Use your 8 to change back to that suit whenever they manage to switch. Track which special cards have been played to know when it's safe to hold a small hand.
tips: In a 2-player game, the Ace (Reverse) acts as a Skipâ€”use it to play two cards in a row.
Pay attention to 'Last One' calls. Catching an opponent and forcing them to draw is the most satisfying way to stall the game.
Don't play your 8 too earlyâ€”it's your insurance policy against being stuck with an unplayable last card.
If you have multiple 2s, consider playing them separately to force consecutive opponents to draw, rather than stacking them on one player.

scoring.description: Penalty point system for cards remaining when another player goes out.
scoring.winCondition: First player to empty their hand wins the round. In multi-round games, lowest cumulative score wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast-paced shedding game from the Crazy Eights family with special penalty cards and the famous 'Last One' announcement rule.
